newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam arms police with new surveillance powers.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam arms police with new surveillance powers.

text.p: Vietnam said on Wednesday it was arming itself with new extra-judicial powers to place citizens under surveillance on grounds of national security.

An official with the central Government Office told Reuters a decree signed earlier this week gave state police the power to monitor people "who cause social disorder", but whose offences were not sufficient to warrant a criminal trial.
"This is one of the means of controlling people involved in fighting, pickpocketing, and other small cases," said the official, who declined to be identified.
He added that police would be responsible for supplying names and details of individuals to provincial and city chiefs, who in turn would authorise the surveillance.

Wednesday's official Quan Doi Nhan Dan (People's Army) newspaper said people under surveillance would be required to live and work in their home localities and undergo education programmes provided by the local authorities.
The decree does not apply to people under the age of 18 and stipulates that the maximum period a person can be subject to surveillance is two years.
Vietnam's existing criminal code allows for police surveillance following conviction by a court.

However, the U.S. State Department noted in its annual report on human rights earlier this year that the government continued "to operate a nationwide system of surveillance and control" through block wardens and informants.
It said anecdotal evidence suggested monitoring was more heavy-handed in Ho Chi Minh City, formerly Saigon.
The Government Office official said the new decree was in line with a National Assembly decision last year on administrative punishments, and was aimed at preventing overcrowding in prisons.
He said the decree would come into effect at the end of April.
